rubric.why: The area under the speed-time graph gives displacement; the graph forms a trapezium.
rubric.description: Uses the trapezium area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Check for the trapezium area expression.

rubric.why: This connects displacement with initial speed, final speed, and time.
rubric.description: Writes displacement as the area of the trapezium.

rubric.why: Uses the definition of acceleration to eliminate time.
rubric.how: Accept either the acceleration relation or its rearrangement.

rubric.why: This is the required third equation of motion.
rubric.description: Derives the third equation of motion.

modelAnswer: In the speed-time graph, displacement s is equal to the area under the graph.
The area is a trapezium: s = ½(u + v)t.
From the definition of acceleration, a = (v − u)/t; therefore, t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting for t: s = ½(u + v)(v − u)/a.
Thus, 2as = (u + v)(v − u) = v² − u².
Therefore, v² = u² + 2as, which is the third equation of motion.
